newsitem.title: FRANCE: Highlights of French Socialist election manifesto.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of French Socialist election manifesto.

text.p: The French Socialist Party manifesto for the May 25-June 1 election, unveiled on Friday, contains the following highlights:
EUROPE

- European monetary union should not exclude EU founder members or EU "pillar" states, EMU vision should not be purely technical, Italy and Spain should be in and Britain if it wants and EMU entry criteria should be read in terms of the trend, as Maastricht treaty says
- euro zone countries should be bound by solidarity and growth pact, not austerity pact
- need for European economic government alongside European Central Bank to coordinate economic policy in interests of democracy
- "We do not want a euro which is overvalued against the dollar and yen"
- Prerequisite for EU enlargement to east is fulfillment of conditions on budget, institutional and agricultural level and should not lead to dismantling of agri, or regional policy
- advance political side of European integration, "No" to erosion of sovereignty, "Yes" to shared sovereignty.
NATIONAL

- create 700,000 jobs, half of them in the public sector and half in private sector, financed without raising spending. Money to come from scrapping of existing job subsidy schemes which it says are ineffective

- gradually cut work week to 35 hours from 39 without loss of salary. manifesto speaks of getting there through negotiation between social partners. (Socialist Party policy maker Dominique Strauss-Kahn spoke in La Tribune on May 2 of cutting work week by law after three years)
- "national conference on jobs, wages and work time"
- research crucial to development, aim to improve budget for research to the equivalent of 2.5 percent of GDP
- help entrepreneurs and small businesses by developing tax system favourable to risk investment for young companies and simplifying administrative procedures
- lowering payroll charges, enlarging/reforming CSG levy
- lowering VAT on goods of primary necessity
- easing housing tax burden on lower income groups
- raising wealth tax to create more just contribution from capital to national solidarity
- reform of social security system aimed at preserving it: control of health spending in negotiated, qualitative fashion and guaranteeing access for low income households to free care
- bolster shared-contribution pensions system, upgrade pensions for poorer people, aligning pensions with net salary
- social housing reform, remodeling post-war housing developments, aims of 300,000 renovated and 150,000 new social housing units per year

- education to be top budget priority with emphasis on positive discrimination in favour of identified education priority zones (ZEPs). raising grants for teacher-training schools and trainee teachers, relaunch of 1988-93 "universite 2000" policy

- preservation of French public service model: security, education, transport, health post and telecoms are services which must be guaranteed to all French people. "We reject the privatisation of public services and turning them into groups devoted to making a profit".

- on immigration, scrap "Pasqua" and "Debre" laws, develop new ways of control with tough penalties for companies which break law and development of cooperation policy with other countries which want to control immigration flows
- improved security, with redeployment/dedication of 50,000 police and other security-related personnel and recruitment of 5,000 police, creation of independent police control agency

- environmentally, public transport a priority, adjust tax on fuels according to pollution criteria, moratorium on nuclear plant construction, closure of "superphenix" fast-breeder reactor, abandoning of Rhine-Rhone-Saone wide canal project
- culture budget target of one percent of GDP, improved access to multimedia, revision/strengthening of aid to press and audiovisual production with aim of helping independent press

- justice system must be independent of politics: appointing of magistrates should no longer be subject to political scrutiny, justice minister should not be allowed in any way intervene in individual judicial proceedings.
- five-year terms for all elective political offices, strict limits on the number of offices any one individual can hold at one time, constitution to enshrine aim of equality between men and women
- decentralisation of state missions
- reestablishing administrative checks/controls on company layoffs
